title: Distinguishing siderophore-associated NRPS genes
question: How can siderophore-associated NRPS genes be distinguished from other NRPS families in fungal genomes?
evidence: Protein domain architecture, sequence similarity, phylogenetic relationships, and conserved genomic context may provide complementary evidence for functional annotation.
hypothesis: Combining multiple independent genomic features may improve functional assignments compared with relying on sequence similarity alone.
alternatives: Similar domain architectures may occur in NRPS enzymes producing different metabolites. Gene-cluster predictions may also be incomplete.
tests: Compare candidate protein sequences, evaluate NRPS domain architectures, construct gene-family phylogenies, and examine available genomic context.
limitations: Sequence-based predictions alone cannot establish the biochemical product of an uncharacterized pathway.

title: Evolutionary history of microbial iron acquisition
question: What can ancient microbial genomes reveal about the evolutionary history of siderophore-associated genes?
evidence: Ancient genomic sequences may provide temporally constrained observations of gene-family presence and sequence variation when authenticity and sample ages are adequately established.
hypothesis: Comparison of well-characterized ancient and modern homologs may improve reconstruction of siderophore gene-family evolutionary histories.
alternatives: Apparent gene absence may reflect incomplete assemblies, differential preservation, or annotation limitations rather than biological gene loss.
tests: Validate genomic provenance and age metadata, identify homologous genes, build gene-family phylogenies, and evaluate uncertainty under alternative evolutionary models.
limitations: Sample ages do not directly establish the origin dates of gene families. Contamination, incomplete recovery, and horizontal gene transfer may complicate inference.

title: Predicting biological responses to molecular change
question: How can genomic variation and molecular mechanisms be integrated to predict biological responses to perturbations?
evidence: Genomic, biochemical, and experimental measurements can provide complementary information about molecular function, but biological responses depend strongly on cellular and environmental context.
hypothesis: Models that integrate mechanistic constraints with evolutionary and experimental data may generate more informative predictions than sequence information alone.
alternatives: Some responses may be dominated by regulatory, physiological, or environmental factors not represented in a sequence-centered model.
tests: Begin with measurable biological phenotypes, establish simple predictive baselines, evaluate uncertainty, and compare predictions against independent experimental observations.
limitations: This is a future research direction, not a validated predictive capability.
